title: Double Pipe Heat Exchanger

introduction.definition: A double pipe heat exchanger has one pipe inside another. The hot fluid flows through the inner tube and the cold fluid through the annulus around it, in opposite directions (counter-current). Heat passes through the inner tube wall. Several hairpins can be connected in series for more area.
key_points: Economical up to ~ 30–50 m² per unit
introduction.summary: A double pipe (hairpin) heat exchanger is the simplest exchanger: one fluid flows in an inner tube, the other in the annulus between it and an outer pipe. Running the two fluids in opposite directions (counter-current) gives the best heat transfer. Hairpins are compact, easy to clean and handle high pressure.

temperature.title: Temperature along the hot stream
temperature.description: Counter-current flow: the hot fluid (inner tube) cools as it travels while the cold fluid in the annulus flows the opposite way and warms up. Counter-flow keeps a temperature difference along the whole length, so it transfers more heat than parallel flow.

foundation: Support on saddles/structure designed for full-of-water weight; allow one end to slide.
alignment: Provide pull-out space for tube bundles or plates; align nozzles to piping without strain.
piping: Install vents and drains on both sides; fit strainers where fouling solids are expected.
commissioning: Pressure-test each side; vent air; bring flows on gradually to avoid thermal shock.

lubrication: No lubrication — static equipment (lubricate valve stems and manway hinges only).

video_tutorials.title: Double Pipe Heat Exchanger — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Double Pipe Heat Exchanger.
A double pipe heat exchanger has one pipe inside another.
The hot fluid flows through the inner tube and the cold fluid through the annulus around it, in opposite directions (counter-current).
Heat passes through the inner tube wall.
Typical applications include small duties and high-pressure services; sludges and viscous fluids (finned/scraped versions); pilot plants and process heating/cooling; lube-oil coolers.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Outer Pipes (Shell Legs) with End Closures.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.

video_tutorials.title: Double Pipe Heat Exchanger — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Double Pipe Heat Exchanger.
Monitor outlet temperatures and ΔP.
Clean tube and annulus (mechanical/chemical).
Hydro-test; replace gaskets/inner tube.
Watch for fouling: falling duty, rising ΔP. Common cause: deposits, scale.
Watch for leak between fluids: contamination. Common cause: tube corrosion, cracked bend.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
